author: GamingBolt
description:
The quality of Nioh 3: Hell Rising will come down to the individual player with a single question: “do you want to play more Nioh 3?” If your answer to this is yes, then Hell Rising is a great excuse to dive back into the game. 

If, however, you wanted more from the base game in terms of narrative and variety, you’re out of luck here, since the DLC continues to deliver the same experience. While the new zone itself is quite fantastic, and there’s plenty of fun to be had with the Hoko & Shield once you get used to its high-risk-high-reward gameplay style, the fact that new Yokai bosses are still lacking, and many of the bosses here are just more humanoids is certainly a disappointment. 

Hell Rising, with its 5 to 8 hour runtime, simply doesn’t feel like it adds enough to Nioh 3 to make it worth the price of admission from anyone aside from die-hard fans of the base game. For everyone else, waiting until the second DLC actually completes the story might be a better option.
title: Nioh 3: Hell Rising DLC Review - Only For The Hardcore Fans

author: GamingBolt
description:
After being delayed from last year, FromSoftware is finally ready to release Elden Ring Tarnished Edition for the Nintendo Switch 2 on August 28th. Of course, we're no stranger to the original – it won tons of Game of the Year awards in its launch year (including our own) and sold tens of millions of copies. To say that it was the most impactful release of 2022 would be an understatement, and it will finally be available for Nintendo fans later this month.

So what should you expect from the package, which retails for a whopping $79.99?
title: Elden Ring Tarnished Edition - 15 Things You Need To Know Before You Buy

author: GamingBolt
description:
The latest developments surrounding GTA 6 are a classic case of hype overriding reason. The impact of Grand Theft Auto 6 on players as a whole – the frenzy for something, anything, new, even if it's just a few months out from launch. 

The anger over locking some in-game stores behind the $100 Ultimate Edition, which didn't stop it from topping pre-orders worldwide over the Standard Edition. It's enough to make fans forget about those working on the title, even if they can still show empathy while criticizing the higher-ups responsible for the marketing strategy they do not appreciate. 

Either way, the Extended Look is still on, and whether it satisfies the ravenous fanbase or not, it's make-or-break for Rockstar. And, we perhaps know, how that is going to turn out.
title: GTA 6 - What The Heck Is Even Going On?
